instructions: Add one confirmed row per concrete evidence item. Cite canonical source files, copy verifier excerpts verbatim, and judge source presence separately from recovery.

criteria.criterion: Use the correct Oyez case page (Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka (1), not Brown II)
criteria.description: Evaluate whether the agent sourced information from the specified Oyez page for Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka (1) (e.g., 347 U.S. 483) and did not substitute Brown II or other sources. Full credit if the agent uses the Brown I page or, if Oyez is inaccessible/blocked, the agent explicitly states it could not access/verify the Brown I page and therefore cannot reliably extract the requested fields. Partial credit if the agent appears to use Oyez but the case version is ambiguous. No credit if the agent clearly uses Brown II or non-Oyez sources in place of the specified page when the Brown I page is accessible.

criteria.criterion: Report all required dates with argued vs. reargued ranges kept distinct
criteria.description: Verify the agent reported (a) argued dates, (b) reargued dates, and (c) decided date from the Brown I Oyez page, keeping argued and reargued ranges distinct. Full credit if all three are present and clearly separated, OR if the agent states the page/dates were inaccessible or did not render despite an attempt. Partial credit if one date field is missing or argued/reargued are present but not clearly distinguished. No credit if dates are wrong/merged with no stated access/rendering limitation.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 1 shows ARGUED: “Dec 9 - 11, 1952”. Screenshot 2 (later) shows REARGUED: “Dec 7 – 9, 1953” and DECIDED: “May 17, 1954”.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: All required dates are present in the agent output, correct, and argued vs. reargued ranges are kept distinct.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The dates section shows “ARGUED” with “Dec 9 - 11, 1952” visible. The “REARGUED” label is visible at the bottom edge of the screenshot, but the reargued date range itself is not shown in the visible portion. The “DECIDED” date is not visible anywhere in this screenshot.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Only the argued date range is verifiable from this screenshot. The agent’s predicted output includes reargued dates (Dec 7–9, 1953) and a decided date (May 17, 1954), but those are not visible here, so they are not supported by this screenshot evidence. Based strictly on what’s shown, the criterion is only partially satisfied/verified.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The agent’s predicted output claims specific reargued dates and a decided date, but this screenshot does not display the reargued date range or any decided date. The argued dates in the output (“December 9–11, 1952”) do match the visible “Dec 9 - 11, 1952”.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence:
The page visibly shows:
- Under “REARGUED”: “Dec 7 – 9, 1953”
- Under “DECIDED”: “May 17, 1954”
The “ARGUED” date range is not visible in the screenshot area provided.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Partial satisfaction. The screenshot supports the agent’s reported reargued dates (Dec 7–9, 1953) and decided date (May 17, 1954). However, the argued date range is not visible, so the screenshot cannot corroborate the agent’s claimed argued dates (Dec 9–11, 1952). The agent did keep argued vs. reargued distinct in their predicted output, but only two of the three date fields are verifiable from this screenshot.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent’s predicted output includes “Argued dates: December 9–11, 1952,” but the screenshot does not show any “ARGUED” label or those dates. Reargued and decided dates match what is visible.

criteria.criterion: Conclusion card decision details (split and prevailing side)
criteria.description: Check that the agent reported both the decision split (vote count) and the prevailing side as shown on the Oyez Conclusion decision card. Full credit if both match the card, OR if the agent indicates the Conclusion card was not accessible/did not load. Partial credit if only one is provided or the source is unclear. No credit if incorrect/invented with no stated access/rendering limitation.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 3 (latest for Conclusion) shows “UNANIMOUS DECISION FOR BROWN ET AL.” No numeric vote split is visible in the provided screenshot evidence.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Agent correctly reported the prevailing side and that it was unanimous, consistent with what is shown. However, the requested ‘decision split’ (vote count) is not provided in the agent output; since it is not evidenced as visible here, only partial credit is warranted for reporting unanimity/prevailing side.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: In the “Conclusion” decision card, the screenshot shows the line: “UNANIMOUS DECISION FOR BROWN ET AL.” No explicit numeric vote split (e.g., 9-0) is visible in this screenshot area.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The agent reported “Unanimous decision for Brown et al.” which matches the visible prevailing-side line. However, the criterion asks for both the split (vote count) and prevailing side. Since the screenshot only shows “UNANIMOUS DECISION…” and not a numeric split, the agent did not provide an explicit vote count; the output is therefore incomplete for the ‘split’ component based on what is shown/required.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Predicted output provides prevailing side but does not provide a numeric split (e.g., 9-0). The screenshot also does not show a numeric vote count, only “UNANIMOUS DECISION FOR BROWN ET AL.”

criteria.criterion: Conclusion card one-line holding immediately below the majority-opinion label
criteria.description: Check that the agent copied the one-line holding that appears immediately below the majority-opinion label on the Oyez Conclusion card, without substituting the longer explanatory paragraph or outside summaries. Full credit if the exact one-line holding is provided, OR if the agent clearly states it could not view/load that one-line holding due to Oyez access/rendering issues (and therefore cannot quote it). Partial credit if nearly exact with small omissions/edits that keep the same sentence structure. No credit if it uses the longer paragraph, paraphrases broadly, or pulls from non-Conclusion/external sources when the one-line holding is accessible.
